assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established that household leverage and mortgage credit expansions drive housing booms, consumption collapses and deep recessions. This changed how macroeconomics and macro-finance understand the origins of the Great Recession and credit cycles. The evidence is empirically credible, uses granular data, and has clear policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: The core joint work on household debt, the 'House of Debt' agenda and credit-supply expansions is centered on Mian and Sufi. Campbell's contributions to household finance and mortgage choice are valuable but not the core of this discovery, so he is not proposed.
assessment.maturity: Key papers are from roughly 2009 to 2015 and have been replicated and extended across countries. The idea is now standard in macro and finance teaching and policy analysis, so timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Partial thematic overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig).
Some debate on the quantitative weight of credit-supply versus other housing-boom explanations.
Whether the committee prefers to also credit Campbell's household-finance contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm trade framework reshaped international trade theory and empirics by showing that selection, productivity differences and reallocation across firms drive the gains from trade. It links closely to firm-level microdata and to growth and productivity research, and has had very wide influence.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman's broader program (with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, and earlier monopolistic competition and trade work) supports his credit. Redding is an important extender and quantifier but is a less essential third name.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation, with a large body of empirical and quantitative work. Krugman's 2008 prize covered earlier new trade theory, so this is a distinct step.
uncertainties: Whether Redding or others (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) should be credited alongside.
Possible overlap with Krugman's earlier trade prize in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Task-based thinking about technology, skill demand and wage inequality, together with the empirical analysis of import-competition shocks and local labour-market adjustment, is among the most influential labour economics of recent decades. It combines conceptual framing with credible research design and has strong policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task-based approach and the China shock work. Hanson is central to the trade-shock evidence. Katz is central to the long-run race between education and technology and the skill-premium literature. Dorn is a key co-author on the trade-shock papers, so the 3-name limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from the late 1990s to the mid 2010s and have been widely replicated and debated. Interpretation has matured.
uncertainties: Partial thematic overlap with the 2024 prize and the 2025 technology-and-growth prize on technology and institutions.
Debate over the persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects.
The 3-name cap forces exclusion of Dorn.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Used population-scale administrative data to measure intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and teacher value-added, opening a new empirical way to study opportunity. It is influential across public, labour and urban economics and in public debate.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual leader. Hendren and Friedman are close collaborators on the neighbourhood and mobility programs. Katz is also credited, but his case is stronger in B014.
assessment.maturity: Major papers are from 2014 to 2022, so this is relatively recent and the long-run follow-up of interventions is still developing. Data-access and replication practices have made the work visible and testable.
uncertainties: Relative recency compared with older candidates.
Questions about causal interpretation of place-based effects and about attribution within a very large collaborator network.
Possible concentration of credit on one person.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, microfounded monetary policy rules and optimal policy analysis underpins modern central banking and macroeconomic modelling. Its practical and academic influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is diffuse. Calvo (pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule), Woodford (systematic theory and optimal policy), Gali (the canonical model and empirics) and Christiano-Eichenbaum (estimated DSGE) are all important. Choosing three names omits several deserving people.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in policy institutions provide strong confirmation, although the 2008 crisis and post-pandemic inflation prompted criticism and extension.
uncertainties: Hard attribution problem with eight credited names and a three-laureate cap.
Prior prizes on rational expectations and macro modelling (Lucas, Sargent-Sims, Kydland-Prescott) partly overlap.
The post-2021 inflation experience makes the verdict on the framework less settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that misallocation of inputs across heterogeneous firms can account for much of cross-country TFP and income differences, giving a quantifiable bridge between micro data and aggregate development outcomes. This sparked a large literature in growth, development and macro.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the central paper. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) is a parallel foundational contribution and Restuccia is credited here, but the two-name proposal reflects the most direct attribution. Disclosure: this member is a long-time co-author of Klenow, so the assessment should be discounted accordingly.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of follow-up and wide use, though the measured size of misallocation is sensitive to measurement error and assumptions.
uncertainties: Personal conflict from co-authorship with Klenow, disclosed but not adjudicated.
Sensitivity of the measured TFP losses to measurement error and model assumptions.
Credit among Restuccia, Rogerson and others is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint mechanism in 'Credit Cycles' shows how asset prices and credit limits amplify and propagate shocks. It is foundational for modern macro-finance and financial-friction models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the core contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist (and Bernanke) developed the financial accelerator, but Bernanke's 2022 prize covered part of that area. Two names best reflect the original idea.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence, with extensive extensions in DSGE models and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on financial crises and with B001.
Whether Gertler should be included given his role in the financial accelerator and in B019.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy, the Redux model and the exchange-rate disconnect puzzles established the microfounded framework of modern international macroeconomics and policy discussion.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the clear joint authors of the core framework (including the textbook and the Redux model). Their separate contributions on exchange-rate puzzles and policy are also important.
assessment.maturity: Work from the 1990s to the 2000s with long-standing influence. Some empirical puzzles remain open.
uncertainties: Rogoff also appears in B043 and could be considered there.
Empirical puzzles remain unresolved, so the framework's final verdict is mixed.
Relative importance compared with domestic macro and finance candidates.
